question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&0&0\\0&3&0\\0&0&4\end{bmatrix}$, find $\operatorname{adj}A$ and verify that $A(\operatorname{adj}A)=|A|I$.
explanation:
Determinant of the diagonal matrix
The determinant is the product of the diagonal entries: $$|A|=(2)(3)(4)=24$$
Adjoint of the matrix
The diagonal cofactors are the products of the other two diagonal entries. All off-diagonal cofactors are zero. Therefore, $$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}12&0&0\\0&8&0\\0&0&6\end{bmatrix}$$
Matrix-product verification
Multiplying, $$A(\operatorname{adj}A)=\begin{bmatrix}24&0&0\\0&24&0\\0&0&24\end{bmatrix}$$
Comparison with $|A|I$
Since this matrix equals $24I=|A|I$, the required identity is verified.
